reviewStandard: Scientific identity, morphology, controlled identifiers, caption limits, non-diagnostic framing, provenance, accessibility, and publication files validated against the WikiBiome scientific media policy.

assets.scientificFinding: NCBI taxonomy identifies the genus and cites the original description as anaerobic Gram-negative diplococci; the selected image shows only paired cocci.
assets.visualReview: Six isolated diplococcal pairs; no rods, flagella, spores, labels, or scene elements.

assets.scientificFinding: Published morphology references describe short pleomorphic coccobacilli that become more coccoid in stationary phase and are nonmotile.
assets.visualReview: Short plump rods, rounded forms, pairs, and one short chain; no flagella.

assets.scientificFinding: NCBI confirms species identity; the reviewed microbiology source describes short pleomorphic, nonmotile coccobacilli.
assets.visualReview: Five coccobacilli with restrained capsular boundaries; no flagella or clinical scenery.

assets.scientificFinding: Actinomycetota is a phylum whose documented forms include coccoid, rod-coccoid, fragmenting hyphal, and branched mycelial morphologies.
assets.visualReview: Four separated representative groupings; the caption explicitly disclaims a single phylum morphology and literal relative scale.

assets.scientificFinding: NLM sources describe nonmotile Gram-positive filamentous rods, sometimes branching, straight or wavy, with swollen or clubbed heads.
assets.visualReview: The first draft was held because fine surface hairs conflicted with nonmotility. Draft v2 removed every appendage-like hair while retaining clean segmented branching rods and clubbed ends.

assets.scientificFinding: Electron microscopy of LF82 documents flagella and type 1 pili, while AIEC remains a functionally defined E. coli pathotype rather than a morphologically diagnostic taxon.
assets.visualReview: Three ordinary bacilli with peritrichous flagella and abundant fine pili on the central cell; caption prevents morphologic overclaiming.
